rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says Joseph took and broke a gold-and-silver idol belonging to his maternal grandfather, then threw it on the road; his brothers taunted him with this.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أنه قال في الآية : سرق يوسف عليه السلام صنما لجده أبي أمه من ذهب وفضة

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: As a boy staying with his maternal uncle, Joseph took a small golden statue from their church; this is what the brothers meant by theft.
rows.anchor: وأخرج غير واحد عن زيد بن أسلم قال : كان يوسف عليه السلام غلاما صغيرا مع أمه عند خال له وهو يلعب مع النعمان

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: A needy visitor came, and Joseph took an egg and handed it to him.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : إن سائلا جاءه يوما فأخذ بيضة فناولها اياه

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Joseph took a chicken and gave it to a beggar.
rows.anchor: وقال سفيان بن عيينة : أخذ دجاجة فأعطاها السائل

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Joseph used to hide food from the table for poor people.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب : كان عليه السلام يخبأ الطعام من المائدة للفقراء

rows.speaker: ابن المنير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Munir calls such accounts an unacceptable slur on the prophetic household and says they should be discarded; Makkī agrees.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن المنير أن ذلك تصلف لايسوغ نسبة مثله إلى بيت النبوة بل ولا إلى أحد من الأشراف فالواجب تركه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the brothers meant another human brother had stolen something similar; they cite hadith parallels and call this interpretation acceptable.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : المعنى إن يسرق فقد سرق مثله من بني آدم وذكر له نظائر في الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author objects that rejecting every theft explanation as scandalous is excessive, since some explanations do not attribute disgraceful conduct to the prophetic house.
rows.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن في عد كل ماقيل في بيان المراد من سرقة الأخ تصلفا فان فيه مالابأس في نسبته إلى بيت النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that إن reflects uncertainty: finding the cup alone did not prove theft, just as the brothers’ goods earlier appeared in their packs without making them thieves.
rows.anchor: وأتوا بكلمة ( إن ) لعدم جزمهم بسرقته بمجرد خروج السقاية من رحله فقد وجدوا من قبل بضاعتهم في رحالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers taking إن as a genuine condition even if the brothers were certain, in view of what follows.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنهم جزموا بذلك ( وإن ) لمجرد الشرط ولعله الاولى لظاهر ما يأتي

rows.speaker: بعض الروايات
rows.claim: One report says they asked Joseph how he could steal; after his denial, he said whoever placed their goods in their packs had placed the cup in his.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الروايات أنهم لما رأوا اخراج السقاية من رحله خجلوا فقالوا : ياابن راحيل كيف سرقت هذه السقاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يسرق narrates a past event as present; they shift disgrace onto Joseph and his full brother. أخ is indefinite because listeners do not know him.
rows.anchor: ( ويسرق ) لحكاية الحال الماضية والمعنى إن كان سرق فليس ببدع لسبق مثله من أخيه

rows.speaker: أحمد بن جبير الأنطاكي وابن أبي سريج والوليد بن حسان
rows.claim: They read فقد سرق with a doubled rāʾ in the passive, meaning Joseph had been accused of theft.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أحمد بن جبير الانطاكي وابن أبي سريج عن الكسائي والوليد بن حسان وغيرهم ( فقد سرق ) بالتشديد مبنيا للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in فأسرها refers to the resentment implied by their words, or to their statement or accusation; Joseph kept it within himself and did not answer them.
rows.anchor: الضمير لما يفهم من الكلام والمقام أي أضمر الحزازة التي حصلت له عليه السلام مما قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not displaying the resentment means neither saying nor doing anything, out of forbearance; أنتم شر مكانا means the brothers are more firmly characterized by theft and slander.
rows.anchor: لا قولا ولا فعلا صفحا لهم وحلما وهو تأكيد لما سبق

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses the next sentence as an explanation of an implicit pronoun, with the feminine reference treated as a sentence or utterance.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : إن الاضمار هنا على شريطة التفسير لأن ( قال أنتم ) الخ بدل من الضمير

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali says an explanatory pronoun must be linked to the preceding clause, whereas the proposed explanation is detached from it.
rows.anchor: وتعقب ذلك أبو علي بأن الاضمار على شريطة التفسير على ضربين أحدهما أن يفسر بمفرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier example explains a sentence by a sentence, while this concerns a sentence explaining a pronoun; al-Kashshaf’s reading makes the quoted clause the explanation, which is obscure.
rows.anchor: وتعقب بأن في تلك الآية تفسير جملة بجملة وهذه فيها تفسير ضمير بجملة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some infer inner speech from treating قال as an appositive to أسر; the author says the conclusion does not depend on that parsing.
rows.anchor: واستدل بعضهم بالآية على اثبات الكلام النفسي بجعل ( قال ) الخ بدلا من أسر

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan takes Joseph to have addressed them aloud after privately resenting their words, to rebuke and contradict them; the author finds this debatable.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : إن الظاهر أنه عليه السلام خاطبهم وواجههم به بعد أن أسر كراهية مقالتهم

rows.speaker: عبدالله وابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: They read فأسره with a masculine pronoun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبدالله وابن أبي عبلة ( فأسره ) بتذكير الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أعلم intensifies God’s knowledge to its utmost degree rather than comparing it with theirs, since they do not know the truth.
rows.anchor: عالم علما بالغا إلى اقصى المراتب بأن الامر ليس كما تصفون

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan reads أعلم comparatively: God knows events’ realities better than the brothers, including how their brother’s theft occurred.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : ان المعنى أعلم بما تصفون به منكم لأنه سبحانه عالم بحقائق الامور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that comparison requires shared knowledge is answered by saying the brothers claimed knowledge for themselves.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأنه تكفي الشركة بحسب زعمهم فانهم كانوا يدعون العلم لأنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: شيخا كبيرا means very old and unable to bear separation, relying on Benjamin for comfort after his full brother’s loss; alternatively it means advanced in age or great in rank.
rows.anchor: طاعنا في السن لا يكاد يستطيع فراقه وهو علالة به يتعلل عن شقيقه الهالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask that one of them be taken in Benjamin’s place because they are not as dear to their father.
rows.anchor: فلسنا عنده بمنزلته من المحبة والشفقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنا نراك من المحسنين may urge the ruler to complete kindness to them or appeal to his general custom of kindness.
rows.anchor: الينا فأتم احسانك فما الانعام الا بالاتمام أو من عادتك الاحسان مطلقا

rows.speaker: بعض المدققين
rows.claim: On the first reading, the kindness clause is a parenthetical conclusion; on the second, it is a general concluding reinforcement.
rows.anchor: والجملة على الوجهين اعتراض تذييلي على ماذهب اليه بعض المدققين

rows.speaker: بعض آخر
rows.claim: Another analysis makes the clause explanatory if it means kindness to them, but emphatic if it describes the ruler’s established habit.
rows.anchor: وذهب بعض آخر إلى أنه إذا أريد بالاحسان اليهم تكون مستأنفة لبيان ماقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: معاذ الله expresses seeking refuge; the verb is omitted and its verbal noun is placed with its object, with the preposition omitted as in similar constructions.
rows.anchor: نعوذ بالله تعالى معاذا من ( أن نأخذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph refuses to take anyone except the person found with the cup because that follows the brothers’ legal ruling, which he will not violate.
rows.anchor: لأن أخذنا له إنما هو بقضية فتواكم فليس لنا الاخلال بموجبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنا إذا لظالمون means unjust according to their law; the royal plural presents the decision as belonging to the ruler and his council.
rows.anchor: في مذهبكم وشرعكم ومالنا ذلك وإيثار صيغة المتكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من وجدنا متاعنا عنده is preferred to the shorter من سرق متاعنا because it mirrors their judgment and states truth without falsely asserting theft.
rows.anchor: وإيثار ( من وجدنا متاعنا عنده ) على من سرق متاعنا الاخصر لأنه أوفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: متاع is useful property, here the cup; the wording is delicate beside أخذ, which can mean enslavement or service, and the taking is apparently literal.
rows.anchor: والمتاع اسم لما ينتفع به وأريد به الصواع وما ألطف استعماله مع الأخذ

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya suggests their offer is rhetorical exaggeration, like asking to be killed to dissuade someone, since a free non-thief cannot lawfully be enslaved.
rows.anchor: وجوز ابن عطية أن يكون ذلك مجازا

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: He also suggests they meant to leave a guarantor until Benjamin returned to tell their father; the author calls the interpretation unreliable.
rows.anchor: أن يريدوا استرقاق حر فلم يبق إلا أن يريدوا بذلك الحمالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s inward reason is that revelation ordered him to retain Benjamin for divine purposes; taking another would wrong himself and oppose revelation.
rows.anchor: إن الله عز وجل إنما أمرني بالوحي أن آخذ بنيامين لمصالح علمها سبحانه في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: استيأسوا means they despaired of Joseph’s answer; the form may simply mean despaired, or its added letters may intensify complete loss of hope.
rows.anchor: أي يئسوا من يوسف عليه السلام واجابته لهم وإلى مرادهم فاستفعل بمعنى فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their complete despair likely followed Joseph’s appeal to God and calling their proposal unjust, signaling strong aversion.
rows.anchor: لما شاهدوه من عوذه بالله تعالى مما طلبوه الدال على كون ذلك عنده في أقصى مراتب الكراهة

rows.speaker: بعض الآثار
rows.claim: A report says Reuben became furious and threatened a cry that would cause Egyptian pregnancies to miscarry; Joseph calmed him through his child, then wrestled him after Reuben challenged the brothers to divide markets and kingship.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الآثار أنهم لما رأوا خروج الصواع من رحله وكانوا قد أفتوا بما أفتوا تذكروا عهدهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take the pronoun in منه to refer to Benjamin, but the author objects that the eldest stayed behind for Benjamin.
rows.anchor: وجوز بعضهم كون ضمير ( منه ) لبنيامين وتعقب بأنهم لم ييأسوا منه

rows.speaker: البزي عن ابن كثير
rows.claim: He reads استأيسوا, deriving it from أيس; the cited morphological argument is that the initial yāʾ did not change to alif.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو ربيعة عن البزي عن ابن كثير أنه قرأ ( استأيسوا ) من أيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خلصوا means they withdrew from others; al-Zajjaj’s gloss that they separated from one another is questioned.
rows.anchor: انفردوا عن غيرهم واعتزلوا الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نجيا means people conferring privately; it is singular because it is a verbal noun that can describe a group or function as an adjective for mutual consultation.
rows.anchor: أي متناجين متشاورين فيما يقولون لأبيهم عليه الصلاة والسلام وإنما وحده

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labid’s line uses أنجية for confidential consultations, supporting the sense of نجيا as a private council.
rows.anchor: قال لبيد : وشهدت أنجية الخلافة عاليا كعبي وأرداف الملوك شهود

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari cites poetry using أنجية for a group consulting privately and notes that the plural is irregular against the expected pattern.
rows.anchor: وأنشد الجوهري : إني إذا ماالقوم كانوا أنجيه واضطربوا مثل اضطراب الارشيه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the eldest brother as Shimon, the leader.
rows.anchor: وهو شمعون قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies the eldest brother as Reuben, the oldest by age.
rows.anchor: وهو روبيل قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: وهب والكلبي
rows.claim: Wahb and al-Kalbi identify the eldest as Judah, greatest in intelligence.
rows.anchor: وهو يهوذا قاله وهب والكلبي

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq identifies the eldest brother as Levi.
rows.anchor: وعن محمد بن إسحاق أنه لاوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pledge is an oath by God, made by God’s permission or from God’s side; ومن قبل means before this, and ما فرطتم may be extra in a circumstantial clause, the soundest parse.
rows.anchor: عهدا يوثق به وهو حلفهم بالله تعالى وكونه منه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative makes ما مصدرية and prior neglect a second object of تعلموا; objections concern separation and fronting, but the author says these constructions are permitted.
rows.anchor: أن تكون ( ما ) مصدرية ومحل المصدرالنصب عطفا على مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse coordinates the phrase with the noun after أن and supplies a predicate such as في يوسف or من قبل; the author finds it contextually weak.
rows.anchor: بجواز العطف على اسم ( أن ) ويحتاج حينئذ إلى خبر

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء وأبو حيان
rows.claim: They cite Sibawayh’s rule that temporal endpoints cannot serve as predicates, complements, adjectives, or circumstantial phrases.
rows.anchor: من أن الغايات لاتقع خبرا ولا صلة

rows.speaker: صاحب الدر المصون
rows.claim: He argues an omitted genitive after an endpoint is allowed when context identifies it, restoring the phrase’s informative force.
rows.anchor: في الدر المصون بأنه إنما امتنع ذلك لعدم الفائدة لعدم العلم

rows.speaker: الشهاب
rows.claim: Al-Shihab notes disagreement: al-Marzouqi allows endpoints as predicates and other complements, while grammarians differ on whether omitted endpoints are definite or indefinite.
rows.anchor: وقال الشهاب : ( 2 ) أن ماذكروه ليس متفقا عليه

rows.speaker: صاحب الدر
rows.claim: The author praises the distinction that an endpoint can inform when its omitted complement is specifically known from context, but not when only a generic complement is recoverable.
rows.anchor: إذا كان معلوما مدلولا عليه بأن يكون مخصوصا معينا صح الإخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other parses treat ما as verbal noun, relative pronoun, or indefinite described noun; on the relative reading, التفريط means prior action from the root meaning to precede, not negligence.
rows.anchor: والتفريط بمعنى التقديم من الفرط لابمعنى التقصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In فلن أبرح الأرض, برح is a complete verb meaning depart or appear, with الأرض as object and Egypt intended; it is not defective or adverbial.
rows.anchor: تامة وتستعمل إذا كانت كذلك بمعنى ذهب وبمعنى ظهر كما في قولهم : برح الخفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eldest stays until his father permits departure or God determines a way out preserving the pledge or freeing Benjamin; divine judgment can even mean death.
rows.anchor: أويحكم الله لي ( بالخروج منها على وجه لايؤدي إلى نقض الميثاق

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan calls the father’s permission particular and God’s judgment general; their order suggests the former is preferred, while the latter supplies any valid excuse.
rows.anchor: غيا ذلك بغايتين خاصة وهي اذن أبيه وعامة وهي حكم الله تعالى له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the best of judges because He judges only with truth and justice.
rows.anchor: إذ لا يحكم سبحانه إلا بالحق والعدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to return and report is apparently a continuation of the eldest brother’s speech; attributing it to Joseph is unlikely.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن هذا القول من تتمة كلام كبيرهم وقيل : هو من كلام يوسف عليه السلام وفيه بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They testify only to what they knew from the cup being found in Benjamin’s pack; they did not know beforehand that he would steal or their father would lose him.
rows.anchor: إلا بما علمنا ( من سرقته

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak reads سارق as an active participle.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك ( سارق ) باسم الفاعل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو رزين والكسائي
rows.claim: They read سُرِّق in the passive, meaning attributed to theft; the brothers did not know whether the cup was stolen or planted unnoticed.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وأبو رزين والكسائي في رواية ( سرق ) بتشديد الراء مبنيا للمفعول

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some praise the passive reading because it avoids asserting actual theft; others say strong presumption can count as knowledge, as in testimony based on established appearances.
rows.anchor: واستحسنت هذه القراءة لما فيها من التنزيه كذا قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says they mean that throughout their lives they testified only to what they knew, and this is a report rather than formal testimony.
rows.anchor: وقيل : معنى ( ماشهدنا ) الخ ما كانت شهادتنا في عمرنا

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf says their certainty is supported by the earlier conditional charge; the author says the dispute is not crucial.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشف الذي يشهد له الذوق انهم كانوا جازمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The obscure interpretation that الغيب means night in Himyaritic is rejected as needlessly opaque; the normal sense is unseen, with lām strengthening the object.
rows.anchor: لليل وهو بهذا المعنى في لغة حمير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والحسن
rows.claim: They identify the village as Egypt; this fits if Joseph himself searched the brothers.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس وقتادة والحسن مصر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some identify a nearby village where the caller caught up with them; this fits if the caller rather than Joseph searched them.
rows.anchor: الأول ظاهر على القول بأن المفتش لهم يوسف عليه السلام والثاني الظاهر على القول بأنه المؤذن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking the village means asking inhabitants by metonymy or omitted genitive; the caravan means owners, a group from Canaan or Sana'a.
rows.anchor: وسؤال القرية عبارة عن سؤال أهلها إما مجازا في القرية

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A literal request to question villages and animals for miraculous speech is rejected as irrelevant to a scene not presenting a miracle.
rows.anchor: لاتجوز ولا اضمار في الموضعين والمقصود احالة تحقيق الحال

rows.speaker: الشهاب
rows.claim: Al-Shihab proposes a rhetorical literal reading: the event is so evident even places and beasts know it; the author says most prefer ellipsis.
rows.anchor: الأولى ابقاء ( القرية والعبر ) على ظاهرهما وعدم اضمار مضاف اليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their emphatic truth claim is not proof of itself; it reinforces their report or expresses customary truthfulness and confidence their father will accept them.
rows.anchor: فيما أخبرناك به وليس المراد اثبات صدقهم بما ذكر حتى يكون مصادرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narration omits the brothers’ report to focus on Jacob’s reply; one account says Joseph sent greetings and predicted the Egyptian king would live to see him.
rows.anchor: وانما حذف للايذان بأن مسارعتهم إلى قبول كلام ذلك القائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بل rejects their implied claim to be blameless, not their factual account; Jacob implies their conduct or ruling led to this outcome, contrary to Egyptian law.
rows.anchor: للأضراب وهو على ماقيل اضراب لا عن صريح كلامهم

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan posits omitted words that بل corrects; Ibn Atiyya calls that apparent, while Ibn al-Munir links Jacob’s suspicion to prior history and Benjamin’s seizure.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حيان إن هنا كلاما محذوفا وقع الاضراب عنه

rows.speaker: ابن المنير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Munir says the brothers did not deliberately wrong Benjamin or misreport events, but their earlier conduct made them suspect to their father.
rows.anchor: وذكر ابن المنير في توجيه هذا القول ههنا مع أنهم لم يعتمدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Finding the cup in baggage alone does not establish theft under law; failure to clarify suggests eagerness to detain Benjamin unless their law made the finding decisive.
rows.anchor: مجرد وجود الصواع في رحل من يوجد في رحله سرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tanwin in أمرا magnifies the matter; فصبر جميل elides a phrase such as my affair is patience. Jacob hopes God will return his three absent sons.
rows.anchor: والتنوين في ( أمرا ) للتعظيم أي أمرا عظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: العليم knows Jacob’s and his sons’ condition, while الحكيم tests and relieves distress according to profound wisdom.
rows.anchor: ( إنه هو العليم ( بحالي وحالهم الحكيم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Jacob’s hope is attributed to Joseph’s earlier dream; he awaited it with trust in God, whose custom brings relief after distress peaks, and the Egyptian king hoped to see Joseph before dying.
rows.anchor: قيل : انما ترجى عليه السلام للرؤيا التي رآها يوسف عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob turns away because of their news and cries for Joseph; أسفا is intense sorrow, and its alif most likely replaces first-person yāʾ for ease.
rows.anchor: كراهة لما جاؤا به ( وقال ياأسفي على يوسف

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: An alternative treats the alif as the alif of lamentation, with an omitted final hāʾ; the author prefers the first analysis.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الألف ألف الندبة والهاء محذوفة والمعول عليه الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob grieves especially for Joseph because that loss was the foundation of later losses and remained vivid; further grief reopened the old wound.
rows.anchor: لأن رزأه كان قاعدة الارزاء عنده وإن تقادم عهده

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam says intense natural love can coexist with love of God and lead to repeated prayer and absorption; another view says Jacob knew the other brothers were alive but lacked a sign about Joseph.
rows.anchor: وقال الامام : إن مثل هذه المحبة الشديدة تزيل عن القلب الخواطر

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: A report says only Muhammad’s community was taught to say إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون at calamity, contrasting this with Jacob; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني وابن مردويه والبيهقي في شعب الايمان عن سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairing of أسفا and يوسف is an elegant, unforced instance of wordplay.
rows.anchor: وفي ( أسفا ) ( ويوسف ) تجنيس نفيس من غير تكلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eyes whiten from grief through crying: grief causes tears and tears cause pigment loss, so the original cause stands for the proximate one.
rows.anchor: وهو في الحقيقة سبب للبكاء والبكاء سبب لابيضاض عينه

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan takes the whitening as a figure for complete blindness, supported by the later statement that Jacob regained sight.
rows.anchor: استظهره أبو حيان لقوله تعالى : ( فارتد بصيرا )

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view says a white film clouded Jacob’s eyes and left him with weak vision; al-Hasan considered blindness permissible for prophets.
rows.anchor: ليس كناية عن ذلك والمراد من الآية أنه عليه السلام صارت في عينيه غشاوة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Jacob grieved eighty years from Joseph’s departure, wept until losing sight, and was then most honored before God.
rows.anchor: كان منذ خرج يوسف من عند يعقوب عليه السلام إلى يوم رجع ثمانون سنة

rows.speaker: ليث بن أبي سليم
rows.claim: A report says Gabriel told Joseph in prison that Jacob’s eyes whitened from grief, quantified it as seventy calamities, and promised one hundred martyrs’ reward.
rows.anchor: عن ليث بن أبي سليم أن جبريل عليه السلام دخل على يوسف عليه السلام في السجن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid read الحزن with fatḥa on both letters; Qatada reads it with ḍamma on both.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ومجاهد ( من الحزن ) بفتح الحاء والزاي وقرأ قتادة بضمهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse supports grief and weeping at calamity; suppressing such reactions may not be fully within a person’s control.
rows.anchor: واستدل بالآية على جواز التأسف والبكاء عند النوائب

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: The two canonical collections report that the Prophet wept for Ibrahim, saying the eyes shed tears and the heart grieves while the tongue says only what pleases God.
rows.anchor: وقد روى الشيخان من حديث أنس أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم بكى على ولده إبراهيم

rows.speaker: أسامة
rows.claim: The two collections report that the Prophet held a dying infant granddaughter, wept, and explained that God placed mercy in chosen servants and shows mercy to the merciful.
rows.anchor: ورويا أيضا من حديث أسامة أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم رفع اليه صبي لبعض بناته

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf cites a reply that the Prophet forbade two foolish cries, at joy and sorrow, not weeping itself.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشاف أنه قيل له عليه الصلاة والسلام : تبكي وقد نهيتنا عن البكاء

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan answered criticism of his grief by noting God did not make grief a disgrace for Jacob.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن أنه بكى على ولد أو غيره فقيل له في ذلك فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كظيم may mean full of anger at his sons but restraining it, or full of grief and concealing it; imagery derives from a tied waterskin or swallowing anger.
rows.anchor: مملوء من الغيظ على اولاده ممسك له في قلبه لايظهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors the active analysis because فعيل regularly works as an active adjective; the image is repeatedly swallowing grief without exposing it.
rows.anchor: ورجح الأخير منهما بأن فعيلا بمعنى فاعل مطرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speakers are the brothers, though some say followers; تفتأ means continue, with negation omitted because the oath lacks markers of affirmation.
rows.anchor: تالله تفتؤ ( أي لاتفتأ ولا تزال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basrans require lām and nūn for affirmative oath replies, so their absence signals negation; Kufans and al-Farisi allow either alone, with examples of deletion in present-tense verbs.
rows.anchor: ولزوم اللام والنون مذهب البصريين وقال الكوفيون والفارسي : يجوز الاقتصار على أحدهما

rows.speaker: خير الدين الرملي
rows.claim: A legal ruling applies this grammar to colloquial oaths: والله أقوم is fulfilled if the speaker rises, but failure to rise does not break the oath, even for someone who does not know Arabic.
rows.anchor: على ما أفتى به خير الدين الرملي وذكر ان الحلف بالطلاق كذلك

rows.speaker: المقدسي
rows.claim: Al-Maqdisi argues common usage should make an unmarked future oath binding on non-fulfillment; he cites the convention that mispronouncing بالله can still form an oath.
rows.anchor: وتعقبه المقدسي بأنه ينبغي أن تلزمهم الكفارة لتعارفهم الحلف كذلك

rows.speaker: الخير الرملي
rows.claim: Al-Ramli says vowel errors do not prevent an oath, but that differs from whether an unmarked response means affirmation or negation; he relies on the transmitted rule.
rows.anchor: واعترضه الخير الرملي بأن مانقله لايدل لمدعاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author distinguishes grammatical mistakes from the disputed affirmative-versus-negative meaning; another reported formula counts as an oath only with intent because it is unfamiliar.
rows.anchor: أما أولا فبأن اللحن كما في المصباح وغيره الخطأ في العربية

rows.speaker: الفاضل الحلبي
rows.claim: Al-Halabi favors present convention: speakers distinguish affirmation from negation by whether لا appears, so customary meaning governs ordinary language.
rows.anchor: وقال الفاضل الحلبي : إن بحث المقدسي وجيه

rows.speaker: السائحاني
rows.claim: Al-Saihānī says current oaths have a recognized new convention; customary language should govern them.
rows.anchor: قال السائحاني : إن أيماننا الآن لاتتوقف على تأكيد

rows.speaker: المقدسي
rows.claim: Al-Maqdisi prefers Abu Yusuf’s interpretation of omitted fāʾ as a condition because omission is common in eloquent Arabic and colloquial usage disregards grammar.
rows.anchor: وفي شرح نظم الكنز للمقدسي أنه ينبغي ترجيح قول أبي يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Oath grammar does not govern divorce and emancipation formulas used as conditional acts; customary meaning makes the consequence follow if the named act occurs.
rows.anchor: ثم أن ما ذكر انما هو في القسم بخلاف التعليق

rows.speaker: الحلبي
rows.claim: Al-Halabi rejects applying oath-response rules to divorce phrases; the lām and nūn rule concerns affirmative oath replies, not conditional clauses.
rows.anchor: قال الحلبي : وبهذا يندفع ما توهمه بعض الافاضل

rows.speaker: أحمد الحموي
rows.claim: A man promised on divorce to complain about his wife’s son by morning but did not; al-Hamawi rules the divorce took effect because the condition failed.
rows.anchor: وقال السيد أحمد الحموي في تذكرته الكبرى : رفع إلي سؤال

rows.speaker: أحمد الحموي
rows.claim: Al-Hamawi condemns the contrary ruling as ignorant: omission rules do not apply to conditional divorce, and failure to complain by morning triggers it.
rows.anchor: فأجبت أنا بعد الحمد الله تعالى ما أفتى به هذا المجيب

rows.speaker: الحلبي
rows.claim: Al-Halabi distinguishes a divine oath from conditional divorce: in the latter, the named act is itself the condition.
rows.anchor: إن إن قام زيد أقم على معنى أن زيد لم أقم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poem illustrates an affirmative response lacking the expected oath markers.
rows.anchor: ولله تعالى در القائل + من الدين كشف الستر عن كل كاذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فتئ is a defective verb like كان; Ibn Malik says it can mean cease or slacken, explaining Mujahid’s gloss about not slackening in love for Joseph.
rows.anchor: هذه من أخوات كان الناقصة كما أشرنا اليه ويقال فيها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats cessation and slackening as associated; Abu Hayyan calls Ibn Malik’s proposal corruption, but the author notes support from al-Farraʾ and al-Sarsaqsti.
rows.anchor: وأوله الزمخشري بأنه عليه الرحمة جعل الفتوء والفتور أخوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse may permit oaths based on strong expectation; alternatively, the brothers knew Jacob’s state but treated him like a denier and reinforced their warning.
rows.anchor: واستدل بالآية على جواز الحلف بغلبة الظن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حرضا means someone sick and near death or consumed by grief; it is a verbal noun used as invariant adjective, while Ibn Ishaq glosses it as corrupt or irrational.
rows.anchor: مريضا مشفيا على الهلاك وقيل : الحرض من اذابه هم

rows.speaker: ابن إسحق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq defines الحرض as corrupt or lacking reason.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن إسحق : الحرض الفاسد الذي لاعقل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading has حرضا with fatḥa on ح and kasra on ر.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( حرضا ) بفتح الحاء وكسر الراء

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri reads حرضا with ḍamma on both letters, like invariant adjectives such as جنب and غرب.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن البصري ( حرضا ) بضمتين ونحوه من الصفات رجل جنب وغرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الهالكين means the dead; أو may mean بل or فلا, or mark alternatives with the more frequent outcome first.
rows.anchor: قيل : يحتمل أن تكون بمعنى بل أو بمعنى فلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بث originally means scattering; it names unbearable grief as though its bearer cannot carry it alone and disperses it for help, a metaphor with passive or active force.
rows.anchor: البث في الاصل اثارة الشيء وتفريقه كبث الريح التراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob says he complains to God alone, seeking refuge and relief, rather than complaining to them or anyone else.
rows.anchor: إني لاأشكو مابي اليكم أو إلى غيركم

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: A report attributes to the Prophet the saying that concealing charity, calamities, and illness are among the treasures of goodness, and broadcasting grief is impatience.
rows.anchor: وفي الخبر عن ابن عمر قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من كنوز البر اخفاء الصدقة

rows.speaker: الحسن وعيسى وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Isa read حزني with fatḥa on both letters; Qatada reads it with ḍamma on both.
rows.anchor: قرأ الحسن وعيسى ( حزني ) بفتحتين وقرأ قتادة بضمتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob knows from God’s grace and mercy what others do not, so hopes God will show kindness; من may explain the knowledge or mark its source.
rows.anchor: من الله ( أي من لطفه ورحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say Jacob knew Joseph was alive from his dream; others say a dream encounter with the Angel of Death confirmed he had not died.
rows.anchor: قيل : إنه عليه السلام علم ذلك من الرؤيا حسبما تقدم

rows.speaker: النضر
rows.claim: Al-Nadr says it reached him that Jacob spent twenty-four years unsure whether Joseph lived until the Angel of Death said he had not taken his soul.
rows.anchor: والمروي عن ابن أبي حاتم عن النضر أنه قال : بلغني أن يعقوب عليه السلام مكث أربعة وعشرين عاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تحسس means seeking information through perception; the distinction that tajassus is evil and tahassus good is rejected because this verse is also read with ج.
rows.anchor: أي فتعرفوا وهو تفعل من الحس وهو في الاصل الادراك بالحاسة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib distinguishes broad sensory awareness from جس, originally feeling a pulse to judge health and illness, and more narrowly investigating a sensed condition.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب : أصل الجس مس العرق وتعرف نبضه للحكم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking news of Joseph and his brother is intended; the eldest is omitted because he chose to stay and would not be hard to locate.
rows.anchor: من يوسف وأخيه ( أي من خبرهما ولم يذكر الثالث

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says تحسست من فلان is not idiomatic and the preposition means عن; another parse makes من partitive.
rows.anchor: عن ابن الانباري أنه لايقال : تحسست من فلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: روح الله means God’s relief; the word originally means breathing and is metaphorically extended to relief.
rows.anchor: من فرجه سبحانه وتنفيسه وأصل معنى الروح بالفتح كما قال الراغب

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبدالعزيز والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: They read روح with ḍamma and interpret it as mercy, likened to spirit because mercy gives life; رحمة and فضل are explanatory, not canonical variants.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن عبدالعزيز والحسن وقتادة ( روح ) بالضم وفسر بالرحمة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya interprets the ḍamma reading as hope in anyone still alive and possessing God-given spirit.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية كأن معنى هذه القراءة لاتيأسوا من حي معه روح الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to investigate and prohibition against despair explain part of Jacob’s prior knowledge and urge the sons to act.
rows.anchor: إرشاد لهم إلى بعض ماأبهم في قوله : ( وأعلم من الله مالا تعلمون )

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the believer expects good from God in hardship and praises Him in ease.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : إن المؤمن من الله تعالى على خير يرجوه في البلاء

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam argues despair implies denying God’s complete power, knowledge, or generosity, each denial being unbelief; some infer despair itself is unbelief.
rows.anchor: وذكر الامام أن اليأس لايحصل إلا إذا اعتقد الانسان أن الاله غير قادر

rows.speaker: الشهاب
rows.claim: Al-Shihab says the verse alone does not prove that despair makes a person an unbeliever; jurists call it major sin and a trait of unbelievers, not unbelief by itself.
rows.anchor: وقال الشهاب : ليس فيها دليل على ذلك بل هو ثابت بدليل آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A believer may despair because he considers his sin too great or himself unworthy of mercy without denying God’s attributes; this does not make the act itself unbelief.
rows.anchor: مع ايمانه بعموم قدرته تعالى وشمول علمه وعظم كرمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despair is absence of hope for mercy; قنوط adds a settled state, while سوء الظن adds expectation of harsher punishment with withheld mercy.
rows.anchor: اليأس عدم أمل وقوع شيء من أنواع الرحمة له والقنوط

rows.speaker: ابن نجيم
rows.claim: Ibn Nujaym reconciles theologians and jurists: theological despair denies mercy’s breadth over sins, while jurists mean despair from magnifying one’s sins.
rows.anchor: وذكر ابن نجيم في بعض رسائله ما به يرجع الخلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jurists’ usage is closer to Prophetic teaching; a report through Ibn Abbas counts despair and feeling safe from divine plotting among major sins with shirk.
rows.anchor: والأوفق بالسنة طريق الفقهاء لحديث الدارقطني عن ابن عباس مرفوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They return to Joseph in obedience to their father; omitting the return signals haste and certainty of compliance.
rows.anchor: بعد ما رجعوا إلى مصر بموجب أمر أبيهم وإنما لم يذكر ايذانا بمسارعتهم

rows.speaker: اليهود
rows.claim: The author reports a Jewish account in which the brothers were first suspected as spies, left Shimon detained, brought Benjamin to Egypt, then returned home after the cup incident to bring Jacob.
rows.anchor: وأنكر اليهود رجوعهم بعد أخذ بنيامين إلى أبيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They address Joseph as العزيز as an honorific for a powerful ruler; the author has not found discussion of whether they knew his personal name.
rows.anchor: خاطبوه بذلك تعظيما له على حد خطابهم السابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الضر means emaciation from severe hunger, and أهل includes their wives and other household members.
rows.anchor: مسنا وأهلنا الضر ( الهزال من شدة الجوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مزجاة describes goods rejected by traders, hence meager or poor quality; reports give wool and ghee, pine products and grain, locust meal and curds, dried game, ropes and packs, or discounted counterfeit coins.
rows.anchor: مدفوعة يدفعها كل تاجر رغبة عنها واحتقارا من أزجيته اذا دفعته وطردته

rows.speaker: أبو صالح وزيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Abu Salih and Zayd ibn Aslam identify the offered goods as pine products and green grain.
rows.anchor: وروى ذلك عن أبي صالح وزيد بن أسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says their goods were counterfeit silver coins accepted only at a reduced value.
rows.anchor: كانت دراهم زيوفا لاتؤخذ إلا بوضيعة وروى ذلك عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets مزجاة simply as small in quantity.
rows.anchor: والمروي عن الحسن تفسيرها بقليلة لاغير

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives مزجاة from a phrase meaning to get through life with little; the author prefers the rejected-goods explanation.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : هي من قولهم : فلان يزجى العيش أي يدفع الزمان

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari rejects Persian or Coptic origins because established Arabic derivation and inflection show the word is Arabic.
rows.anchor: وتعقب ذلك ابن الانباري بأنه لاينبغي أن يجعل لفظ معروف الاشتقاق

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read مزجية with imāla because its underlying form contains yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي ( مزجية ) بالامالة لأن أصلها الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers mention hardship first to stir compassion, then ask for a full measure; the verse does not prove measuring is the seller’s obligation.
rows.anchor: قدموا هذا الكلام ليكون ذريعة إلى إسعاف مرامهم ببعث الشفقة

rows.speaker: الضحاك وابن جريج
rows.claim: They say تصدق علينا means favor them by returning Benjamin to his father, using charity figuratively for a favor.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك وابن جريج إنهم أرادوا تصدق علينا برد أخينا بنيامين

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan objects to asking God for charity since the giver seeks reward; the author replies with a Prophetic report that God gave the community charity to accept.
rows.anchor: قول الحسن لمن سمعه يقول : اللهم تصدق على إن الله تعالى لايتصدق

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyan ibn Uyayna holds the ban on receiving charity applies to earlier prophets and families; the author says it may cover only obligatory alms.
rows.anchor: كما ذهب اليه سفيان بن عيينة بل هي عامة له عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes the request plainly: after describing hardship they ask Joseph for charity; the author finds this best matched to the setup.
rows.anchor: كما قال الزمخشري : أنهم تمسكنوا له عليه السلام بقولهم : ( مسنا ) الخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may ask for acceptance of poor goods, leniency in exchange, or an added amount; God rewards those who give generously.
rows.anchor: ظاهره بالايفاء أو بالمسامحة وقبول المزجاة
